plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure. Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate. Add QQQI to 25% and QQQ to 20% to favor income and broad index exposure. Trim SMH to zero as it is flagged for trimming. Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but also limits upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure. Trim SPY to 25% to meet concentration mandate. Trim CRWD to 10% and SMH to zero to reduce concentration and exit flagged position. Buy CRWV at 4% and NVDA at 4% to add high-scoring tech setups.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while selectively adding high-quality tech setups, balancing growth with risk management.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet concentration mandate. Trim SMH to 10% to reduce flagged position and reallocate. Add SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to increase leveraged ETF exposure. Buy CRWV at 6%, NVDA at 5%, and PLTR at 5% to concentrate in high-scoring tech setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring tech, leading to higher potential returns but also substantially greater drawdown risk and daily decay from leveraged products.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure. Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate. Trim CRWD to 5% to reduce high-beta single name exposure. Add QQQI to 30% to prioritize income. Trim SMH to zero as it is flagged for trimming. Add QQQ to 15% to maintain some broad index exposure.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on steady monthly distributions. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by cutting leverage and high-beta names, but growth potential is minimal and distributions are variable, not guaranteed.
